phase3_findings.description: The sed runnability probe (printf 'x' | sed -E 's/x/x/') does not compile the program shape this diff introduces (a capture group carrying an alternation under a {4,} interval), and never checks that a redaction actually happened. A reduced sed that passes the probe but cannot compile or correctly apply the real rule is reported through the input-fault message 'sed exited non-zero on the input', mis-attributing a permanent host condition to one payload.
phase3_findings.rationale: Fail direction is unchanged and correct — nothing is emitted, so there is no leak. The probe shape is pre-existing and the raised dialect requirement is plain POSIX ERE, supported by BSD sed (verified locally by replaying every new assertion) and GNU sed (CI's platform). The finding is a real operability improvement but not a merge blocker and is outside issue #1915's scope; better filed as follow-up work.

phase3_findings.description: The twelve new assertions capture stdout through command substitution, so scrub-credentials.sh's success-path exit status is never asserted; only the fail-closed arm is covered (indirectly, via build-denial-record.sh with a stubbed failing sed).
phase3_findings.rationale: Marginal under this project's 'add a test only for a clear important benefit' convention; the fail-closed contract is already exercised. Cheap to add if the fix loop wants it, but not blocking.

phase3_findings.rationale: Not diff-modified and true as written, so not a documented_falsehood; behavior-inert prose, capped at Suggestion under Phase 4.1.5. The final-pass reviewer independently reached the same dismissal. A one-clause extension of that paragraph would close it cheaply.

report:
APPROVE. Iteration 4 of the fix loop on PR #1921 (issue #1915). The diff is small and self-consistent: scripts/scrub-credentials.sh switches its two Authorization rules to a '#' sed delimiter, replaces the class-with-literal-backslash by an alternation of class members plus the escape units \/ and \\, raises + to {4,}, and matches both scheme keywords per letter; lib/test/run.sh adds thirteen behavioural assertions; coverage-map.json registers the run_sh_blocks entry; a changeset discloses the deliberate narrowing.

Four Phase-3 agents were dispatched (code-reviewer excluded by its iterations=first-only override on iteration 4; type-design-analyzer gated out with no new types). No Critical and no Important findings. Three Suggestions were returned, none blocking: an unchanged-but-now-under-covering sed runnability probe whose diagnosis message mis-attributes a host dialect failure to the input (fail direction still closed, no leak), an unasserted success-path exit status in the new block, and a contract-header paragraph that does not mention the scheme keyword now matches per letter too.

I replayed all thirteen new assertions directly against the shipped helper and all thirteen pass; the round-trip JSON fixture parses and is byte-identical to the expected document. The two consumers (scrub-transcript.sh, build-denial-record.sh) call the helper unchanged, no workflow carries an inline mirror of these rules, and the module that exercises the scrub end-to-end (review-trigger-helpers, 844 assertions) is green — its #409 fixtures all use tokens well above the new four-unit floor. shellcheck, ruff, the carve-out guard, the tree-enumeration lint, the reference-size lint and the coverage-map guard are all clean. Every acceptance criterion on issue #1915 is satisfied.

The three prior push-backs carried in the handoff stand: I found no new evidence against the escape-unit closure, the block placement, or the //gI over-redaction (which fails safe). Note the whole-suite completion gate is not discharged by this engine pass — on the local tier that is a CI reading for the commit the run pushes.
